    - name: customer360__email
      description: Unique customer emails per customer360_id with a deterministic 1-based index ordered by email ascending
      grain: One row per unique (customer360_id, email)
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read customer-to-system ID links from marts.customer360__mapping (uses: customer360_id, marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id). - Collect emails from each source via inner joins to mapping: - Marketo: mapping.marketo_lead_id = marketo.lead_id - Stripe: mapping.stripe_customer_id = stripe.customer_id - Zendesk: mapping.zendesk_user_id = zendesk.user_id - Exclude rows where the source email is NULL; preserve original casing and spacing; do not trim or normalize. - Union all collected rows across sources. - De-duplicate to a unique set of (customer360_id, email) using exact string equality. - For each customer360_id, sort emails ascending by their literal value (default lexicographic order) and assign a contiguous 1-based sequential index; output customer360_id, email, and index. - If a customer has no non-NULL emails in any source, no row is emitted for that customer.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 ID from mapping; groups emails and defines the partition for indexing; no explicit NULL filtering
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email from Marketo/Stripe/Zendesk via mapping joins; NULLs excluded; duplicates removed by exact string equality; casing and whitespace preserved without normalization
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Contiguous 1-based sequential index within each customer360_id after sorting emails ascending; stable given the same deduplicated email set
    - name: customer360__ip_address
      description: Latest Marketo IP address per customer360_id based on updated_at
      grain: One row per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping (customer360_id, marketo_lead_id)
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo (lead_id, ip_address, updated_at)
      business_logic: '- Build the customer-to-Marketo mapping from marts.customer360__mapping (customer360_id ↔ marketo_lead_id). - Join to intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on marketo_lead_id = lead_id. - Exclude rows where ip_address is NULL; customers without any non-NULL IP do not appear in the output. - For each customer360_id, sort candidate rows by updated_at descending and assign a rank starting at 1. - Select the single row with rank = 1 per customer360_id: - This corresponds to the most recent updated_at for that customer. - If multiple rows share the same updated_at, the chosen row is unspecified because no tie-breaker is defined. - NULL placement in sorting uses the database default; if all updated_at are NULL for a customer, one NULL row is chosen arbitrarily. - Output columns come from the selected row: customer360_id (from mapping), ip_address (from Marketo), source_system (constant ''marketo''), last_seen (Marketo updated_at).'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 identifier used to group rows and select the most recent Marketo IP
      - name: ip_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: IP address from the chosen Marketo row; preserved as stored; never NULL due to filtering; selection in update-time ties is arbitrary
      - name: source_system
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant 'marketo' for all rows
      - name: last_seen
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: updated_at from the chosen Marketo row (the most recent per customer360_id; tie and NULL ordering follow the database default)
    - name: customer360__mapping
      description: Customer identity mapping linking unified and organizational hashes to source system records and an organization-level header row with aggregated metadata
      grain: 'Mixed: individual rows per combined source record (is_organization_header=false) and one header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true)'
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '1) Load four inputs: source_matches, marketo, stripe, zendesk. 2) Build combine_all_results: - Chain full outer joins: source_matches to marketo on lead_id, then to stripe on customer_id from source_matches, then to zendesk on user_id from source_matches, retaining all records from every source. - For IDs, prefer the value from source_matches when present; otherwise use the corresponding source table value. - Per-row timestamps: - marketo_updated_at = the most recent non-null updated_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - marketo_created_at = the earliest non-null created_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - stripe_updated_at / stripe_created_at = the stripe timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from stripe. - zendesk_updated_at / zendesk_created_at = the zendesk timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk. - zendesk_organization_* = the zendesk organization timestamps from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk.organization_*. - Union in three additional sets to also include any marketo/stripe/zendesk records whose IDs are not present in source_matches; these rows carry only their own system fields, others null. This can yield duplicates relative to the full outer joins. 3) For each row, derive customer360_organization_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo org name without suffix, marketo inferred org name without suffix, stripe customer org name without suffix, stripe shipping org name without suffix, zendesk organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings. 4) Emit two row types: - Individual rows (is_organization_header=false): include the three source IDs; source_ids is a compact JSON-like object {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} where null IDs are rendered as empty strings; timestamps are the per-row values from step 2. - One organization header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true): source IDs are null; source_ids is a JSON-like object with arrays per system containing distinct quoted IDs for that organization (comma-delimited, no spaces), with nulls rendered as empty strings; timestamps aggregated per organization as latest updated_at and earliest created_at for each system; zendesk organization timestamps use latest for updated and earliest for created. 5) Assign customer360_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, is_organization_header, customer360_organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings and using the engine’s string form of the boolean.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_lead_id|stripe_customer_id|zendesk_user_id|is_organization_header|customer360_organization_id with nulls as empty strings and the engine’s string form of the boolean.
      - name: customer360_organization_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_org_name_no_suffix|marketo_inferred_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_customer_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_shipping_org_name_no_suffix|zendesk_organization_id with nulls as empty strings.
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else marketo; null on organization header rows.
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else stripe; null on organization header rows.
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else zendesk; null on organization header rows.
      - name: is_organization_header
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: 'Row type flag: false for individual rows; true for the single aggregated header row per customer360_organization_id.'
      - name: source_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'JSON-like string; individual rows: {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} with nulls as empty strings; header rows: arrays per system of distinct quoted IDs joined by commas (no spaces), nulls as empty strings, order not enforced.'
      - name: marketo_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: latest non-null updated_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: latest marketo_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: marketo_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: earliest non-null created_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: earliest marketo_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: latest stripe_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: earliest stripe_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest zendesk_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest org updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest zendesk_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest org created_at in the organization; null if none.'
    - name: customer360__name
      description: Deduplicated customer full names from Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk with lexicographic variant indexing per customer360_id
      grain: One row per unique full_name per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Start from marts.customer360__mapping to relate customer360_id to source system identifiers. - Collect name candidates via inner joins, excluding rows where the source name is NULL: - Marketo: join by lead ID; use full_name_clean. - Stripe (customer): join by customer ID; use customer_name_clean. - Stripe (shipping): join by customer ID; use shipping_name_clean. - Zendesk: join by user ID; use full_name_clean. - Union all candidates from all sources; any temporary source or index flags used during collection are ignored. - Deduplicate to unique (customer360_id, full_name) pairs; duplicates within a customer are removed, across customers are preserved. - For each customer360_id, sort remaining full_name values in ascending lexicographic order under the database’s default collation and assign a sequential index starting at 1. - Output columns: customer360_id, full_name, index.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer key; one row per unique full_name within each customer360_id.
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name taken as-is from upstream cleaned fields; NULLs are excluded, empty strings may appear; deduplicated per customer360_id; the exact string determines ordering for index.
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Sequential position within each customer360_id after deduplication, starting at 1 and ordered by full_name ascending; consecutive integers with no gaps; not based on source priority.
    - name: customer360__organization
      description: Distinct organization names per customer360_id, alphabetically indexed after consolidating Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk sources
      grain: One row per distinct organization_name per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read marts.customer360__mapping to obtain customer360_id and source identifiers: - marketo_lead_id → intermediate.int_customer360__marketo.lead_id - stripe_customer_id → intermediate.int_customer360__stripe.customer_id - zendesk_user_id → intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk.user_id - Collect organization names via inner joins; exclude rows where the selected name is NULL: - Marketo: organization_name_no_suffix; Marketo inferred: inferred_organization_name_no_suffix - Stripe: customer_organization_name_no_suffix; Stripe shipping: shipping_organization_name_no_suffix - Zendesk: organization_name - Union all collected names across sources. - Deduplicate by exact string equality on (customer360_id, organization_name); casing and whitespace are preserved (no trimming or normalization). - Assign final index as the alphabetical position per customer360_id by ordering organization_name ascending using the database’s default collation; indices start at 1 and are contiguous. - Output customer360_id, organization_name, index.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 identifier from mapping used to group and index organizations; never NULL due to inner joins
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: organization_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name from Marketo (no_suffix or inferred no_suffix), Stripe (customer or shipping no_suffix), or Zendesk; NULL names are excluded; duplicates removed per customer360_id by exact string match; original casing and spacing kept; used for alphabetical indexing
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Alphabetical rank within the deduplicated organization_name list for the customer360_id; starts at 1, contiguous, ordered by organization_name ascending; unrelated to any source-specific priority
        tests:
        - not_null
    - name: customer360__organization_network
      description: Organization-level network, value, health, engagement, risk, ranking, and strategy metrics grouped by standardized_org_name + email_domain (INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER excluded)
      grain: One row per (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      - marts.customer360__customer_value_analysis
      business_logic: '- Build organization_entities: - Join behavior_analysis to lifecycle_metrics on primary_email; join behavior_analysis to value_analysis on primary_email. - Retain ids (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id), journey/segment fields, LTV/health/engagement fields. - Standardize fields: - standardized_org_name: uppercase and trim primary_organization; if null/blank set "INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER". - email_domain: take the substring after "@" in primary_email; if missing set "unknown.domain". - organization_type by primary_organization text patterns: - null/blank → Individual - contains inc/corp/llc/ltd → Corporation - contains university/college/school → Education - contains government/dept/agency → Government - contains nonprofit/foundation/charity → Non-Profit - otherwise → Business - estimated_org_size: - domain in {gmail.com,yahoo.com,hotmail.com,outlook.com} → Personal - domain in {microsoft.com,google.com,amazon.com,apple.com,facebook.com} → Enterprise - else if name length > 20 → Large Business; > 10 → Medium Business; > 0 → Small Business; otherwise → Individual - Aggregate to organization_aggregates at (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size): - Counts (distinct primary_email): total_contacts; marketing_contacts when marketo_lead_id present; sales_contacts when stripe_customer_id present; support_contacts when zendesk_user_id present. - Journey distribution: full_journey_contacts when journey pattern = "Full Journey"; also compute marketing_to_sales_contacts and sales_to_support_contacts (used downstream). - Value metrics: total_organization_ltv (sum of estimated_customer_ltv), avg_customer_ltv, highest_customer_ltv (max), total_adjusted_ltv (sum). - Engagement/health: avg_engagement_score (average composite_engagement_score), max_engagement_score (max), avg_health_score (average customer_health_score). - Strategic classification: strategic_accounts, key_accounts, growth_accounts, recovery_accounts from strategic_classification. - Revenue tiers: tier1_contacts, tier2_contacts, tier3_contacts from revenue_tier. - Customer segments: champions, loyal_customers, at_risk_customers from customer_segment. - Lifecycle stages (for health calc): growth_stage_contacts when stage = "Growth"; maturity_stage_contacts when stage = "Maturity"; dormant_contacts when stage = "Dormant". - Diversity: email_domains_count = distinct email_domain within the group (will be 1); customer_tiers_represented = distinct customer_tier. - Compute organization_scoring: - organization_value_score: weighted sum of three 1–5 tiers, rounded to two decimals (stored with one-decimal precision): - LTV tier: ≥50000→5; ≥25000→4; ≥10000→3; ≥5000→2; else→1 (weight 0.4). - Contacts tier: ≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥3→3; ≥2→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - Avg engagement tier: ≥4.0→5; ≥3.0→4; ≥2.5→3; ≥2.0→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - organization_health_score: 0.4×avg_health_score + 0.3×(champions+loyal_customers)/total_contacts×5 + 0.3×(growth_stage_contacts+maturity_stage_contacts)/total_contacts×5; if total_contacts=0, both ratios are 0; round to two decimals. - account_penetration_score: share of contacts linked across marketing, sales, and support out of three touchpoints, scaled to a 0–5 score and rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0. - organization_maturity: - if total_contacts≥10 and full_journey_contacts≥3 → Mature Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥5 and (strategic_accounts+key_accounts)≥2 → Developing Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥3 and total_organization_ltv≥10000 → Mid-Market - else if total_contacts≥2 → Small Business - else → Individual/Micro - growth_potential: - if growth_accounts≥2 and avg_engagement_score≥3.0 → High Growth Potential - else if growth_accounts≥1 or avg_engagement_score≥3.5 → Medium Growth Potential - else if total_contacts≥2 and avg_health_score≥3.0 → Stable Growth Potential - else → Limited Growth Potential - organization_risk_level: - if at_risk_customers ≥ 50% of total_contacts → High Risk - else if dormant_contacts ≥ 30% of total_contacts → Medium Risk - else if recovery_accounts ≥ 1 → Attention Needed - else → Stable - strategic_value_tier: - if strategic_accounts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥100000 → Strategic Enterprise - else if key_accounts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥50000 → Key Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥5 or total_organization_ltv≥25000 → Important Account - else if total_contacts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥10000 → Standard Account - else → Small Account - engagement_breadth_percentage: weighted coverage across marketing (30%), sales (40%), and support (30%) among contacts, expressed as a percentage and rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0. - concentration_risk: - if total_contacts=1 → High Concentration Risk - else if total_contacts≤3 → Medium Concentration Risk - else if email_domains_count=1 and total_contacts≥5 → Domain Concentration Risk - else → Low Concentration Risk - Perform network_analysis: - market_share_within_type: percent share of total_organization_ltv within the same organization_type, rounded to four decimals; null when the type total is zero. - Rankings within organization_type: ltv_rank_within_type by total_organization_ltv descending; contacts_rank_within_type by total_contacts descending; value_score_rank_within_type by organization_value_score descending; ties break arbitrarily. - cross_sell_opportunity_score (integer 0–7): sum of three components, then rounded (remains integer): - Channel gap: if total_contacts≥5 and marketing_contacts=0 →3; else if total_contacts≥3 and sales_contacts=0 →3; else if total_contacts≥2 and support_contacts=0 →2; else →0. - Growth: High Growth Potential →2; Medium Growth Potential →1; else →0. - Engagement: avg_engagement_score≥3.5 →2; ≥3.0 →1; else →0. - expansion_priority: - if strategic_value_tier in {Strategic Enterprise, Key Enterprise} and growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Immediate Expansion - else if organization_value_score≥4.0 and organization_health_score≥4.0 → High Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥3 and avg_engagement_score≥3.0 → Medium Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥2 and organization_risk_level=Stable → Low Priority Expansion - else → Maintenance Mode - recommended_strategy: - if organization_risk_level=High Risk → Risk Mitigation & Recovery - else if strategic_value_tier=Strategic Enterprise → White Glove Account Management - else if strategic_value_tier=Key Enterprise → Dedicated Account Management - else if growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Growth & Expansion Focus - else if total_contacts=1 → Relationship Expansion - else → Standard Account Management - Finalization: - organization_influence_score: weighted score rounded to two decimals = 0.3×organization_value_score + 0.3×contacts tier (≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥3→3; ≥2→2; else→1) + 0.2×breadth tier (≥80→5; ≥60→4; ≥40→3; ≥20→2; else→1) + 0.2×market-share tier (≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥2→3; ≥1→2; else→1). - risk_adjusted_organization_value: total_adjusted_ltv multiplied by expansion priority multiplier (Immediate 1.5; High 1.3; Medium 1.1; else 1.0), then reduced by risk penalty (High Risk 40%; Medium Risk 20%; Attention Needed 10%; else 0%), rounded to two decimals. - network_analysis_timestamp: set to the current timestamp at computation time. - Exclude rows where standardized_org_name = "INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER". - Order output by organization_influence_score (desc), then total_organization_ltv (desc), then total_contacts (desc).'
      columns:
      - name: standardized_org_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Uppercased, trimmed organization name from behavior_analysis; null/blank becomes 'INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER' and is excluded from final output
      - name: email_domain
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Substring after '@' in primary_email; if missing set to 'unknown.domain'
      - name: organization_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived from primary_organization patterns: Individual, Corporation, Education, Government, Non-Profit, or Business'
      - name: estimated_org_size
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Size class from email_domain and name length: Personal, Enterprise, Large/Medium/Small Business, or Individual'
      - name: organization_maturity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Mature Enterprise if contacts≥10 and full_journey≥3; Developing Enterprise if contacts≥5 and strategic+key≥2; Mid-Market if contacts≥3 and org LTV≥10000; Small Business if contacts≥2; else Individual/Micro
      - name: strategic_value_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Strategic Enterprise if strategic≥2 or org LTV≥100000; Key Enterprise if key≥2 or org LTV≥50000; Important if contacts≥5 or org LTV≥25000; Standard if contacts≥2 or org LTV≥10000; else Small
      - name: total_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of primary_email within the group
      - name: marketing_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a marketo_lead_id present
      - name: sales_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a stripe_customer_id present
      - name: support_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a zendesk_user_id present
      - name: email_domains_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of email_domain within the group; equals 1 due to grouping by email_domain
      - name: customer_tiers_represented
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of customer_tier values within the group
      - name: total_organization_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of estimated_customer_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: total_adjusted_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Sum of adjusted_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: avg_customer_ltv
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of estimated_customer_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: highest_customer_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)

      - name: organization_value_score

      - name: organization_influence_score

        description: Weighted score from value score, contacts tier, engagement breadth tier, and market share tier; rounded to two decimals
      - name: avg_engagement_score

        description: Average composite_engagement_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: max_engagement_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Maximum composite_engagement_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: avg_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average customer_health_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: organization_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted composite of avg_health_score and stage/segment ratios using total_contacts as denominator; rounded to two decimals
      - name: account_penetration_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Scaled 0–5 score of contact presence across marketing, sales, and support relative to all contacts; rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0
      - name: engagement_breadth_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted coverage across marketing (30%), sales (40%), and support (30%) as a percentage; rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0
      - name: full_journey_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_journey_pattern is 'Full Journey'
      - name: strategic_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Strategic Account'
      - name: key_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Key Account'
      - name: growth_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Growth Account'
      - name: recovery_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Recovery Account'
      - name: champions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'Champion'
      - name: loyal_customers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'Loyal Customer'
      - name: at_risk_customers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'At Risk'
      - name: tier1_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 1 - Strategic'
      - name: tier2_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 2 - High Value'
      - name: tier3_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 3 - Core'
      - name: organization_risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Risk label based on at-risk share, dormant share, and recovery_accounts presence
      - name: concentration_risk
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact concentration label from total_contacts and email_domains_count, with a domain concentration flag when only one domain and contacts≥5
      - name: growth_potential
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Growth label from growth_accounts and avg_engagement_score, with stable or limited when thresholds not met
      - name: cross_sell_opportunity_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Integer 0–7 from the sum of channel gap, growth, and engagement components; rounding does not change the integer value
      - name: expansion_priority
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Priority label from strategic tier and growth potential, then value/health scores, then engagement and stability
      - name: recommended_strategy
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Strategy label based on risk level, strategic tier, growth potential, and contact count
      - name: market_share_within_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent share of total_organization_ltv within the same organization_type; rounded to four decimals; null when the type total is zero
      - name: ltv_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by total_organization_ltv descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: contacts_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by total_contacts descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: value_score_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by organization_value_score descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: network_analysis_timestamp
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp captured at computation time
    - name: customer360__phone
      description: Distinct phones with extensions collected from Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk, deduplicated per customer and assigned a per-customer index ordered by phone ascending.
      grain: One row per (customer360_id, phone, extension)
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Use marts.customer360__mapping to link each customer360_id to source records. - For each source, inner join via mapped IDs and collect phone fields only when the phone is not NULL; keep values as-is (no trimming or normalization): - Marketo: phone/phone_extension, company_phone/company_phone_extension, mobile_phone/mobile_phone_extension via mapping.marketo_lead_id = marketo.lead_id. - Stripe: phone/phone_extension, shipping_phone/shipping_phone_extension via mapping.stripe_customer_id = stripe.customer_id. - Zendesk: phone/phone_extension via mapping.zendesk_user_id = zendesk.user_id. - Combine all collected phones across sources without altering values; any per-source index or source label is not retained. - Remove duplicates by exact match of (customer360_id, phone, extension); NULL extensions are allowed and treated as equal for duplicate checking. - Per customer360_id, assign a sequential index starting at 1 based on phone sorted ascending; extension does not affect sort; ties where phone strings are identical (with different extensions) have unspecified order; indices are contiguous with no gaps. - Output columns: customer360_id, phone, extension, index.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer 360 identifier; phones are grouped and indexed per customer.
      - name: phone
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Phone string from sources; NULL phones are excluded; value is preserved; used for deduplication and ascending sort for indexing.
      - name: extension
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Optional phone extension; included in deduplication; not used for sorting.
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Per-customer sequential index starting at 1 after deduplication, ordered by phone ascending; tie order for identical phone strings is unspecified; no gaps.
    - name: customer360__status
      description: Unified customer communication preferences and account status aggregated across Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk
      grain: One row per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Start from marts.customer360__mapping to relate customer360_id to source IDs (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id). - Marketo: - Inner join mapping → intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on marketo_lead_id = lead_id. - Carry is_unsubscribed, is_email_invalid, do_not_call from Marketo as-is. - Derive per-row source_system = ''marketo'' and status: unsubscribed if is_unsubscribed is TRUE; else email_invalid if is_email_invalid is TRUE; else do_not_call if do_not_call is TRUE; else active. - Stripe: - Inner join mapping → intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on stripe_customer_id = customer_id. - Set is_unsubscribed, is_email_invalid, do_not_call to FALSE. - Derive per-row source_system = ''stripe'' and status: delinquent if is_delinquent is TRUE; else deleted if is_deleted is TRUE; else active. - Zendesk: - Inner join mapping → intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on zendesk_user_id = user_id. - Set is_unsubscribed, is_email_invalid, do_not_call to FALSE. - Derive per-row source_system = ''zendesk'' and status: suspended if is_suspended is TRUE; else deleted if is_deleted is TRUE; else inactive if is_active is FALSE; else active. - Union all rows from the three systems. - Aggregate by customer360_id: - For each of is_unsubscribed, is_email_invalid, and do_not_call: take the logical OR across all rows (TRUE if any TRUE; FALSE if none TRUE and at least one FALSE; NULL only if all inputs are NULL). Stripe and Zendesk always contribute FALSE. - overall_status precedence: 1) unsubscribed if the aggregated unsubscribe flag is TRUE; 2) email_invalid if the aggregated email_invalid flag is TRUE; 3) active if any per-row status is active; 4) suspended if any per-row status is suspended; 5) delinquent if any per-row status is delinquent; 6) otherwise inactive. Note: per-row statuses deleted and do_not_call never map directly to the final status. - source_systems: concatenate the distinct source_system values present using ", " as the delimiter; remove duplicates; do not enforce ordering. - Output one row per customer360_id that appears in at least one of the three joined systems.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer surrogate key; exactly one output row per customer360_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: is_unsubscribed
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: TRUE if any contributing row is TRUE; FALSE if none TRUE and at least one FALSE (Stripe/Zendesk contribute FALSE); NULL only if all inputs are NULL
      - name: is_email_invalid
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: TRUE if any contributing row is TRUE; FALSE if none TRUE and at least one FALSE (Stripe/Zendesk contribute FALSE); NULL only if all inputs are NULL
      - name: do_not_call
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: TRUE if any contributing row is TRUE; FALSE if none TRUE and at least one FALSE (Stripe/Zendesk contribute FALSE); NULL only if all inputs are NULL
      - name: overall_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Final status with precedence: unsubscribed > email_invalid > active (if any) > suspended (if any) > delinquent (if any) > inactive; values limited to {unsubscribed, email_invalid, active, suspended, delinquent, inactive}'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: source_systems
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma+space separated distinct list of contributing systems; duplicates removed; ordering unspecified; never NULL
        tests:
        - not_null
    - name: customer360__summary
      description: Summary per customer360_id with first-ranked profile fields joined to all IP address records.
      grain: One row per customer360_id per ip_address record; if any ranked source has multiple index=1 or rank=1 rows for an id, rows multiply accordingly; if no ip_address exists, one row per customer360_id.
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - marts.customer360__email
      - marts.customer360__phone
      - marts.customer360__name
      - marts.customer360__organization
      - marts.customer360__address
      - marts.customer360__ip_address
      business_logic: '- Use marts.customer360__mapping as the base set keyed by customer360_id. - From each profile source, keep only rows marked as first-ranked: - Email, Phone, Name, Organization: rows where the index equals 1. - Address: rows where the rank equals 1. If none exist for an id, the joined values are NULL. If multiple rows satisfy the first-ranked condition for an id, all are kept and will multiply output rows. - Left join the ranked subsets to mapping on customer360_id. - Left join marts.customer360__ip_address on customer360_id without ranking or de-duplication; each ip_address record produces a separate output row. - Emit selected fields exactly as stored in sources; no additional sorting, distinct, trimming, normalization, or formatting is applied. Nulls arise naturally from left joins.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary key from mapping used to join all sources; row multiplicity follows the joins described.
      - name: source_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Value taken verbatim from mapping.
      - name: customer360_organization_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization identifier from mapping.
      - name: is_organization_header
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Boolean flag from mapping indicating the organization header record.
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email from the email source where the id’s index equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: phone
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Phone from the phone source where the id’s index equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from the name source where the id’s index equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: organization_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name from the organization source where the id’s index equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: address_line_1
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary address line from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: address_line_2
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Secondary address line from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: city
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: City from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: State or region from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: country
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Country from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: country_alt_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Alternative country name from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: postal_code
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Postal code from the address source where the id’s rank equals 1; NULL if no such row.
      - name: ip_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: IP address from all matching ip_address records; NULL if none.
    - name: customer360__updates
      description: Per-customer summary of updates from Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk, showing latest and earliest timestamps, total updates, and distinct source/type lists.
      grain: One row per customer360_id that has at least one joined update from any source
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read customer-to-source IDs from marts.customer360__mapping (customer360_id, marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id). - Create update rows via inner joins: - Marketo: join mapping.marketo_lead_id to intermediate.int_customer360__marketo.lead_id; take updated_at as last_updated and created_at as first_seen; set source_system=''marketo'' and update_type=''lead_update''. - Stripe: join mapping.stripe_customer_id to intermediate.int_customer360__stripe.customer_id; take updated_at as last_updated and created_at as first_seen; set source_system=''stripe'' and update_type=''customer_update''. - Zendesk: join mapping.zendesk_user_id to intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk.user_id; take updated_at as last_updated and created_at as first_seen; set source_system=''zendesk'' and update_type=''user_update''. - Union all per-source rows; duplicates are preserved. - Aggregate by customer360_id: - last_updated: the latest non-null last_updated across all rows; returns null if all are null. - first_seen: the earliest non-null first_seen across all rows; returns null if all are null. - total_updates: the count of all joined rows across sources; includes duplicates and rows with null timestamps. - updated_by_systems: concatenate distinct source_system values with ", "; case preserved; nulls excluded; no guaranteed ordering. - update_types: concatenate distinct update_type values with ", "; case preserved; nulls excluded; no guaranteed ordering. - Output includes only customers with at least one joined update row.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique customer identifier; one row per value.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: last_updated
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest non-null update timestamp across sources; null if none.
      - name: first_seen
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest non-null creation timestamp across sources; null if none.
      - name: total_updates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of joined update rows across sources; includes duplicates and rows with null timestamps.
      - name: updated_by_systems
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Distinct source systems concatenated with ', '; order not guaranteed; case preserved; nulls excluded.
      - name: update_types
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Distinct update types concatenated with ', '; order not guaranteed; case preserved; nulls excluded.

```

## Task Description:
You are a professional Data Engineer responsible for implementing a complete SQL data pipeline based on data contract documents.

## Objectives
Populate the SQL files in the `./sql/` directory according to the specifications in `docs/data_contract.yaml` and `config/layer_dependencies.yaml`. Your task is clear: write the necessary SQL code to ensure `run.py` executes successfully.

You MUST carefully review the content of `docs/data_contract.yaml`. You may use tools to view it. Since the file content is long, you can view it in chunks. Your task is to complete the SQL file writing based on the content of this file.

## Project Background
* Raw data has been loaded into `xxxx_start.duckdb` (Note: 'xxxx' is a placeholder for the project name, such as `greenhouse_start.duckdb` or `google_ads_start.duckdb`; 'xxxx' appearing below carries the same meaning).
* Currently, running `python run.py` completes the data transformation and outputs `xxxx.duckdb`.
* The existing SQL project is stored in the `sql/` folder.
* The current requirements documentation is located in `docs/data_contract.yaml`.

**Implementation Requirements:**
1. **Strictly Adhere to Configuration**:
    * All SQL logic and dependencies must be written strictly according to the `staging`, `intermediate`, and `marts` hierarchy defined in the YAML configuration files.

2. **File and Directory Structure**:
    * SQL files must be created in the corresponding level subdirectories (e.g., `sql/staging/`, `sql/intermediate/`, `sql/marts/`).
    * Strictly follow predefined file naming conventions and coding styles.

3. **Use Pure DuckDB Syntax**:
    * All SQL code must be compatible with DuckDB.
    * **Do NOT** end SQL statements with a semicolon (`;`) at the end of the file.

4. **No dbt Syntax**:
    * You must reference upstream tables directly using the `schema.table_name` format.
    * **Do NOT** use the dbt `ref()` function.

    **Examples**:
    * **Correct ✅**:
```sql
    with account_base as (
    select *
    from staging.stg_salesforce__account
    where not is_deleted
    ),

    account_enriched as (
    select
    account_id,
    ...
```

* **Incorrect ❌**:
```sql
    WITH accounts AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM {{{{ ref('stg_salesforce__account') }}}}
    ),
    contacts AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM {{{{ ref('stg_salesforce__contact') }}}}
    ),
    ...
```
Output Standard: Ensure the generated SQL files can be successfully executed by run.py to produce high-quality data results that meet business requirements.


## Contract file paths:
- ./docs/data_contract.yaml

## Data Contract Documentation (docs/data_contract.yaml):

```yaml
version: "1.0"
metadata:
  description: "Complete data pipeline specification for Customer360 system - transforming raw customer data from multiple sources into unified customer profiles"
  author: "Data Engineering Team"
  created_date: "2025-09-08"
  pipeline_phases: ["staging_contract", "modeling_spec"]
  source_systems: ["Marketo", "Stripe", "Zendesk"]
  business_purpose: "Create unified customer 360-degree view for marketing, sales, and support operations"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# PHASE 1: Defines the transformation from raw data to clean staging tables.  #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
staging_contract:
  purpose: "Transform raw data into clean, validated staging tables with standardized formats, data quality validation, and reference data enrichment. This phase focuses on data cleansing, format standardization, and basic validation without business logic application."
  
  quality_actions:
    correct:
      description: "Automatically fix deterministic format issues such as email casing, whitespace trimming, and standardized date formats"
      examples: ["LOWER(TRIM(email))", "standardize timezone formats", "normalize phone numbers"]
    
    delete_row:
      description: "Remove entire row when records contain severe data quality issues that make them unusable downstream."
      examples: ["Explicitly marked for deletion", "Confirmed duplicates", "Invalid primary keys", "Essential business attributes contain irrecoverable errors"]
    
    nullify_field:
      description: "Set invalid field values to NULL when the field is non-critical and record can still be useful"
      examples: ["malformed optional URLs", "invalid secondary contact information", "corrupted metadata fields"]

  tables:
    # Reference Data Tables
    - name: stg_customer360__country_codes
      description: "Standardized country code reference data supporting ISO 3166 standards for geographic data validation and normalization"
      source_table: raw.country_codes
      columns:
        - name: country_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(TRIM(country_name)) > 0"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: alternative_country_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
        - name: country_code_numeric
          data_type: INTEGER
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "country_code_numeric BETWEEN 1 AND 999"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: country_code_alpha_2
          data_type: VARCHAR(2)
          constraints: [not_null, unique]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(country_code_alpha_2) = 2"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_2 = UPPER(TRIM(country_code_alpha_2))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_2 ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: country_code_alpha_3
          data_type: VARCHAR(3)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(country_code_alpha_3) = 3"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_3 = UPPER(TRIM(country_code_alpha_3))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_3 ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'"
              on_failure: delete_row

    - name: stg_customer360__state_territory_codes
      description: "Standardized state and territory code reference data with country relationships for address validation"
      source_table: raw.state_territory_codes
      columns:
        - name: state_territory
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: state_code
          data_type: VARCHAR(5)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(TRIM(state_code)) BETWEEN 2 AND 5"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "state_code = UPPER(TRIM(state_code))"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: alpha2_country_code
          data_type: VARCHAR(2)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(alpha2_country_code) = 2"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "alpha2_country_code = UPPER(TRIM(alpha2_country_code))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "regexp_matches(alpha2_country_code, '^[A-Z]{2}$')" 
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "alpha2_country_code IN (SELECT country_code_alpha_2 FROM stg_customer360__country_codes)"
              on_failure: delete_row

    - name: stg_customer360__nicknames
      description: "Name variant mapping table for customer identity matching and name standardization"
      source_table: raw.nicknames
      columns:
        - name: canonical_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "canonical_name = TRIM(canonical_name)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: nickname
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "nickname = TRIM(nickname)"
              on_failure: correct


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# PHASE 2: Defines the business logic from staging tables to analytical models. #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
modeling_spec:
  purpose: "Transform staging data into business-ready models that implement customer identity resolution, data enrichment, and analytical structures for Customer360 insights. This phase applies complex business logic, performs identity matching across systems, and creates comprehensive customer profiles."
  
  design_principles:
    intermediate_purpose: "Create reusable, business-centric data models that implement identity resolution logic and data enrichment patterns. Intermediate models serve as building blocks for final mart models."
    marts_purpose: "Deliver analysis-ready data structures optimized for business intelligence, reporting, and analytical workflows with consistent grain and comprehensive business context."
    identity_resolution: "Implement probabilistic matching across email addresses, names, and organizational affiliations to create unified customer identities."
    data_enrichment: "Enhance customer profiles with standardized geographic data, name variants, and derived attributes."

  intermediate_models:
    - name: int_customer360__marketo
      description: Marketo leads passed through from raw.marketo_leads with non-empty emails and timestamps cast
      grain: One row per raw.marketo_leads record where email IS NOT NULL and email != ''
      source_models:
      - raw.marketo_leads
      business_logic: '- Read all rows from raw.marketo_leads. - Select the listed columns exactly as in the source; no joins, aggregations, or de-duplication; duplicates are preserved. - Keep only records where email is neither NULL nor an empty string; emails containing only whitespace are retained because no trimming is applied. - Cast updated_at and created_at to TIMESTAMP; all other fields are passed through unchanged from source. - Nulls from the source are preserved for all pass-through columns. - No specific row ordering is applied.'
      columns:
      - name: lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Lead identifier from source; duplicates may exist
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email address used for filtering; must be non-null and not empty; case and whitespace preserved
      - name: email_address_stripped
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Standardized email from source
      - name: email_domain
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email domain from source
      - name: full_name_clean
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Cleaned full name from source
      - name: first_name_clean
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Cleaned first name from source
      - name: last_name_clean
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Cleaned last name from source
      - name: name_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Name title from source
      - name: name_suffix
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Name suffix from source
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from source
      - name: first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: First name from source
      - name: last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Last name from source
      - name: organization_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name from source
      - name: organization_name_no_suffix
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name without suffix from source
      - name: organization_name_suffix
        data_type: VARCHAR

      description: Email-based identity matches across Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk with coalesced IDs and combined timestamps (overall latest/earliest across systems and preferred-source values).
      grain: One row per merged match of (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id) produced by full outer joins of the pairwise email matches; duplicates may occur when inputs contain multiple rows for the same email.

      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe_for_matching

      business_logic: '- Build three pairwise match sets using exact email equality (no normalization): - Marketo↔Stripe on identical email. - Marketo↔Zendesk on identical email. - Stripe↔Zendesk on identical email. - Merge matches: - Full outer join Marketo↔Stripe with Marketo↔Zendesk on Marketo lead ID. - Full outer join the result with Stripe↔Zendesk when either Stripe customer ID matches or Zendesk user ID matches. - Derive IDs: - Marketo lead ID: take the Marketo ID from the Marketo↔Stripe match when present; otherwise from the Marketo↔Zendesk match. - Stripe customer ID: take the Stripe ID from the Marketo↔Stripe match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match. - Zendesk user ID: take the Zendesk ID from the Marketo↔Zendesk match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match. - Derive timestamps: - Overall updated_at (named marketo_updated_at): choose the latest non-null among the Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk updated_at values available from the merged matches. - Stripe updated_at: take the Stripe updated_at from the Marketo↔Stripe match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - Zendesk updated_at: take the Zendesk updated_at from the Marketo↔Zendesk match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - Zendesk organization updated_at: take from the Marketo↔Zendesk match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - Overall created_at (named marketo_created_at): choose the earliest non-null among the Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk created_at values available from the merged matches. - Stripe created_at: take the Stripe created_at from the Marketo↔Stripe match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - Zendesk created_at: take the Zendesk created_at from the Marketo↔Zendesk match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - Zendesk organization created_at: take from the Marketo↔Zendesk match when present; otherwise from the Stripe↔Zendesk match; null when neither exists. - No aggregation, sorting, or deduplication is applied; all resulting rows are retained and nulls are handled by selecting the first available or by taking latest/earliest across systems as described.'

    - name: int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      description: Customer behavior profile per resolved customer with cross-platform engagement, lifecycle metrics, and segmentation
      grain: One row per source match key (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id) with non-null primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: 'Build per-customer behavior and segmentation by: - Source inputs: - Marketo (intermediate.int_customer360__marketo) per lead_id - Stripe (intermediate.int_customer360__stripe) per customer_id - Zendesk (intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk) per user_id - Identity map (intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches) providing the cross-platform ID linkage - Per-platform metrics: - Marketo: - marketo_first_touch = created_at; marketo_last_activity = updated_at - marketo_engagement_score: - 0 if is_unsubscribed = true or is_email_invalid = true - else 3 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 2 if < 90 - else 1 - has_organization_data = 1 if organization_name_no_suffix not null and length > 3 else 0 - has_phone_contact = 1 if phone or mobile_phone present else 0 - address_completeness_score: - 3 if country_code, state_code, and city all present - 2 if country_code present and at least one of state_code or city present - 1 if only country_code present - 0 otherwise - Stripe: - stripe_first_transaction = created_at; stripe_last_activity = updated_at - stripe_engagement_score: - 0 if is_deleted = true - 1 if is_delinquent = true (and not deleted) - else 4 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 3 if < 90 - else 2 - payment_reliability_score: - 3 if is_delinquent = false and is_deleted = false - 1 if is_delinquent = true and is_deleted = false - 0 otherwise - billing_completeness_score: - 2 if customer_address_line_1 and customer_country_code present - 1 if only customer_country_code present - 0 otherwise - Zendesk: - zendesk_first_contact = created_at; zendesk_last_activity = updated_at - zendesk_engagement_score: - 0 if is_suspended = true or is_deleted = true - 1 if is_active = false - else 4 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 3 if < 90 - else 2 - org_relationship_strength: - 2 if organization_id and organization_name_no_suffix present - 1 if only organization_id present - 0 otherwise - Join and aggregate: - Left join per-platform metrics to source_matches on respective IDs - primary_email = coalesce(Marketo.email, Stripe.email, Zendesk.email); rows with NULL primary_email are excluded - email_domain and primary_organization use the same COALESCE order (Marketo, then Stripe, then Zendesk) - customer_first_touchpoint = the earliest of the three per-platform first-touch timestamps - customer_last_activity = the latest of the three per-platform last-activity timestamps - If any of the three timestamps is NULL, the earliest/latest result is NULL - marketo_engagement/stripe_engagement/zendesk_engagement = respective per-platform scores with NULL → 0 - composite_engagement_score = weighted average (weights: Marketo 0.3, Stripe 0.5, Zendesk 0.2), rounded to two decimals and stored with one decimal precision - in_marketo/in_stripe/in_zendesk = 1 if respective joined record exists, else 0 - organization_data_quality = coalesce(has_organization_data,0) + coalesce(billing_completeness_score,0) + coalesce(org_relationship_strength,0) - has_contact_phone = coalesce(has_phone_contact, 0) - address_data_quality = coalesce(address_completeness_score,0) + coalesce(billing_completeness_score,0) - marketing_to_sales_days = days between Marketo first touch and Stripe first transaction only if both present; else NULL - sales_to_support_days = days between Stripe first transaction and Zendesk first contact only if both present; else NULL - account_age_days = days between the earliest available first-touch and current_date; NULL if the earliest is NULL - customer_maturity (derived from the same earliest timestamp vs current_date): - ''New Customer'' if < 90 days - ''Growing Relationship'' if < 365 days - ''Established Customer'' if < 1095 days - ''Long-term Customer'' otherwise (including when the start date is NULL) - customer_journey_pattern based on platform presence, evaluated in this order: - ''Full Journey'' if all three present - ''Marketing to Sales'' if Marketo and Stripe - ''Sales to Support'' if Stripe and Zendesk - ''Marketing to Support'' if Marketo and Zendesk - ''Marketing Only'' if only Marketo - ''Sales Only'' if only Stripe - ''Support Only'' if only Zendesk - ''Unknown'' otherwise - payment_reliability = coalesce(Stripe.payment_reliability_score, 0) - Classification: - customer_segment (first match wins): - ''Champion'' if composite_engagement_score >= 3.5 and payment_reliability >= 2 - ''Loyal Customer'' if composite_engagement_score >= 3.0 and customer_journey_pattern = ''Full Journey'' - ''Potential Loyalist'' if composite_engagement_score >= 2.5 and payment_reliability >= 2 - ''New Customer'' if composite_engagement_score >= 2.0 and account_age_days < 90 - ''At Risk'' if composite_engagement_score >= 1.5 - ''Hibernating'' if composite_engagement_score > 0 - ''Lost'' otherwise - churn_risk_level: - ''High Risk'' if payment_reliability = 0 or composite_engagement_score < 1 - ''Medium Risk'' if composite_engagement_score < 2 and account_age_days > 365 - ''Medium Risk'' if customer_last_activity is more than 90 days ago - ''Low Risk'' otherwise (including when comparisons evaluate to NULL) - recommended_action based on customer_segment: - ''Upsell/Cross-sell'' for ''Champion'' or ''Loyal Customer'' - ''Engagement Campaign'' for ''Potential Loyalist'' - ''Onboarding Focus'' for ''New Customer'' - ''Win-back Campaign'' for ''At Risk'' - ''Reactivation Campaign'' for ''Hibernating'' - ''Recovery Campaign'' otherwise - Output filter and ordering: - Keep only rows where primary_email is not NULL - Order rows by composite_engagement_score descending, then account_age_days descending'
      columns:

      - name: payment_reliability

    - name: int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      description: Customer lifecycle metrics, health scoring, retention/churn risk, and cohort/tier enrichments derived from customer behavior analysis
      grain: One row per customer from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis (one row per resolved customer), compute lifecycle metrics and enrichments: - Activity windows and recency: - days_since_last_activity = number of days between customer_last_activity and today; NULL if customer_last_activity is missing. - active_X_days flags (X ∈ {30,60,90,180,365}) = 1 if customer_last_activity occurred within X days of today, else 0; missing customer_last_activity yields 0. - Lifecycle stage (first match wins): - ''Acquisition'' if account_age_days ≤ 30 - ''Activation'' if account_age_days ≤ 90 and last_activity within 30 days - ''Growth'' if account_age_days ≤ 365 and last_activity within 60 days - ''Maturity'' if account_age_days > 365 and last_activity within 90 days - ''Dormant'' if last_activity older than 180 days - Else ''Retention'' - Note: NULL account_age_days or last_activity causes earlier conditions to fail and typically falls through to ''Retention''. - Cohort and platform consistency: - acquisition_cohort_month = month of the first touchpoint (truncated to month); NULL if first_touchpoint is missing. - platform_consistency_score ∈ {1,2,3}: sum of presence flags (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); 3 if sum ≥ 3, 2 if sum = 2, else 1. NULL in any flag leads to the else path → 1. - Value and engagement scores: - estimated_customer_value (DECIMAL(6,2)) by customer_segment: - ''Champion'' 5000.00; ''Loyal Customer'' 3500.00; ''Potential Loyalist'' 2000.00; ''New Customer'' 800.00; ''At Risk'' 1200.00; ''Hibernating'' 500.00; else 200.00. - frequency_score (1–5): 5 if platform_consistency_score = 3 and active_30_days = 1; 4 if platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 and active_60_days = 1; 3 if platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 and active_90_days = 1; 2 if active_180_days = 1; else 1. - recency_score (1–5) by days_since_last_activity: 5 (≤7), 4 (≤30), 3 (≤60), 2 (≤180), else 1; NULL days_since_last_activity maps to 1. - estimated_transaction_count (DOUBLE): simulated per run: - If segment in (''Champion'',''Loyal Customer'') → integer 2–9 - If ''Potential Loyalist'' → integer 1–4 - Else → integer 0–1 - Stored as DOUBLE; values vary each execution. - customer_health_score (DECIMAL(15,2)) = rounded to 2 decimals from: recency_component*0.3 + platform_consistency_score*0.3 + segment_component*0.4, where: - recency_component: 5/4/3/2/1 as in recency_score logic - segment_component: ''Champion'' 5.0; ''Loyal Customer'' 4.5; ''Potential Loyalist'' 3.5; ''New Customer'' 3.0; ''At Risk'' 2.0; ''Hibernating'' 1.5; else 1.0 - Advanced lifecycle metrics: - estimated_customer_ltv (DECIMAL(18,2)) = estimated_customer_value × (1 + 0.2 × frequency_score) × (1 + 0.1 × platform_consistency_score) × stage_factor; rounded to 2 decimals, where stage_factor: Growth 1.5; Maturity 2.0; Retention 1.8; Activation 1.2; else 1.0. - retention_probability (DECIMAL(3,2)) by customer_health_score: ≥4.5→0.95; ≥4.0→0.85; ≥3.5→0.75; ≥3.0→0.65; ≥2.5→0.50; ≥2.0→0.35; else 0.20. - churn_probability (DECIMAL(3,2)) inverse mapping: ≥4.5→0.05; ≥4.0→0.15; ≥3.5→0.25; ≥3.0→0.35; ≥2.5→0.50; ≥2.0→0.65; else 0.80. - revenue_at_risk (DECIMAL(9,2)) = estimated_customer_value × churn-probability mapping above; rounded to 2 decimals. - growth_potential (first match wins): - ''High Growth Potential'' if lifecycle_stage in (''Acquisition'',''Activation'') and customer_health_score ≥ 3.5 - ''Expansion Ready'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Growth'' and platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 - ''Upsell Candidate'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Maturity'' and customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 - ''Stable Account'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Retention'' and customer_health_score ≥ 3.0 - ''Reactivation Needed'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Dormant'' - Else ''Monitor'' - action_priority (INT, first match wins): - 5 if churn-probability mapping ≥ 0.65 - 4 if lifecycle_stage = ''Acquisition'' and customer_health_score ≥ 3.5 - 4 if lifecycle_stage = ''Growth'' and platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 - 3 if customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 and estimated_customer_value ≥ 3000 - 3 if churn-probability mapping ≥ 0.35 - Else 2 - acquisition_year = year of acquisition_cohort_month; acquisition_month = month number; months_since_acquisition = whole months between acquisition_cohort_month and today; NULL if acquisition_cohort_month is NULL. - acquisition_season: ''Holiday Season'' if month in (11,12,1); ''Summer Season'' if in (6,7,8); ''Spring Season'' if in (3,4,5); else ''Fall Season'' (default for NULL or not matched). - Final enrichments: - customer_tier by estimated_customer_ltv: Platinum (≥8000), Gold (≥5000), Silver (≥2500), Bronze (≥1000), else Basic. - is_strategic_account = TRUE if estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 10000 OR (customer_segment in (''Champion'',''Loyal Customer'') AND platform_consistency_score = 3); else FALSE. - intervention_urgency by action_priority: 5→''Immediate''; 4→''This Week''; 3→''This Month''; else ''Routine''. - expected_retention_rate by LTV and lifecycle: 0.90 if LTV ≥ 8000; 0.85 if LTV ≥ 5000; 0.75 if LTV ≥ 2500 and lifecycle_stage ≠ ''Dormant''; 0.60 if LTV ≥ 1000 and lifecycle_stage in (''Growth'',''Maturity''); else 0.45. - performance_vs_expectation: ''Above Expectation'' if retention_probability > expected_retention_rate; ''Meeting Expectation'' if retention_probability ≥ 80% of expected_retention_rate; else ''Below Expectation''. - Output ordering: sorted by is_strategic_account (true first), then action_priority descending, then estimated_customer_ltv descending, then customer_health_score descending.'

      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: 'Build engagement_risk_scoring: - Input rows from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis (ba) left joined to intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (lm) on primary_email. - Compute days_since_last_activity as the number of days between ba.customer_last_activity and today; set to NULL if ba.customer_last_activity is missing. - activity_decline_risk: >90 days → 3; >60 days → 2; >30 days → 1; otherwise → 0. - platform_abandonment_risk from presence across Marketo/Stripe/Zendesk (ba.in_marketo + ba.in_stripe + ba.in_zendesk): sum = 1 → 2; sum = 2 → 1; otherwise → 0. - lifecycle_transition_risk: Dormant → 3; Retention with customer_health_score < 3.0 → 2; Acquisition/Activation with days_since_last_activity > 30 → 2; otherwise → 0. - email_engagement_risk (only if marketo_lead_id is present): days_since_last_activity > 60 → 2; else if composite_engagement_score < 2.0 → 1; otherwise → 0; if marketo_lead_id is missing → 0. Build payment_risk_scoring: - Left join intermediate.int_customer360__stripe (s) on ers.stripe_customer_id = s.customer_id. - payment_behavior_risk precedence: is_delinquent = true → 3; else if is_deleted = true → 4; else if estimated_customer_ltv > 5000 and churn_probability > 0.5 → 2; otherwise → 0. - account_stability_risk: stripe customer exists and days between created_at and updated_at < 30 → 1; else if is_deleted = true → 3; otherwise → 0. - revenue_at_risk_score precedence: LTV ≥ 10000 and churn ≥ 0.5 → 4; else if LTV ≥ 5000 and churn ≥ 0.5 → 3; else if LTV ≥ 2000 and churn ≥ 0.7 → 2; else if churn ≥ 0.8 → 1; otherwise → 0. Build support_risk_scoring: - Left join intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk (z) on prs.zendesk_user_id = z.user_id. - support_engagement_risk precedence: suspended → 3; else if deleted → 2; else if active = false → 2; else if user present and last_update was > 90 days ago → 1; otherwise → 0. - org_relationship_risk: missing organization_id with non-missing primary_organization → 1; else if suspended with organization_id present → 2; otherwise → 0. - satisfaction_risk_score precedence: segment in (''At Risk'',''Hibernating'',''Lost'') → 2; else if churn_risk_level = ''High Risk'' → 3; else if lifecycle_stage = ''Dormant'' and zendesk_active = false → 2; otherwise → 0. Build comprehensive_risk_assessment: - total_risk_score = weighted sum of seven risk components (weights: 0.2 activity_decline, 0.15 platform_abandonment, 0.15 lifecycle_transition, 0.1 email_engagement, 0.25 payment_behavior, 0.1 account_stability, 0.05 revenue_at_risk), rounded to 2 decimals. - risk_category from the unweighted sum S of the seven components: S ≥ 8 → Critical; S ≥ 5 → High; S ≥ 3 → Medium; S ≥ 1 → Low; otherwise → Minimal. - primary_risk_factor precedence: Payment Issues; else Engagement Decline; else Lifecycle Transition; else High Value at Risk; else Support Issues; else Communication Breakdown; else Standard Monitoring. - risk_trend precedence: days_since_last_activity ≤ 7 with customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 → Improving; else if days_since_last_activity ≤ 30 with churn_probability < 0.3 → Stable; else if 30 < days_since_last_activity ≤ 60 → Declining; else if days_since_last_activity > 60 → Deteriorating; otherwise → Unknown. - potential_revenue_loss = estimated_customer_ltv × churn_probability, rounded to 2 decimals. - intervention_timeline precedence: payment_behavior_risk ≥ 3 → Immediate (24h); else if activity_decline_risk + platform_abandonment_risk + lifecycle_transition_risk ≥ 5 → Urgent (1 week); else if revenue_at_risk_score ≥ 3 → High Priority (2 weeks); else if activity_decline_risk + email_engagement_risk ≥ 3 → Medium Priority (1 month); otherwise → Standard Priority. - recommended_intervention precedence: Account Management Call; else Executive Outreach (activity_decline_risk ≥ 2 and LTV ≥ 5000); else Customer Success Check-in; else Personalized Email Campaign; else Product Adoption Workshop; else Lifecycle-specific Campaign; otherwise Automated Monitoring. - intervention_success_probability from S (same sum used for risk_category): S ≥ 8 → 0.30; S ≥ 5 → 0.60; S ≥ 3 → 0.80; S ≥ 1 → 0.90; otherwise → 0.95. Build final_risk_assessment: - customer_priority_score = (risk_category score × 0.6) + (LTV bracket score × 0.4), then rounded; risk_category scores: Critical=5, High=4, Medium=3, Low=2, Minimal=1; LTV brackets: ≥10000=5, ≥5000=4, ≥2000=3, ≥1000=2, else=1. Note: logic rounds to 2 decimals; stored with one-decimal precision per column type. - risk_adjusted_customer_value = estimated_customer_ltv × (1 − churn_probability) × intervention_success_probability, rounded to 2 decimals. - critical_alert_flag = payment_behavior_risk ≥ 3 OR revenue_at_risk_score ≥ 4. - high_value_at_risk_flag = activity_decline_risk ≥ 2 AND estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 3000. - engagement_warning_flag = platform_abandonment_risk ≥ 2 AND customer_health_score < 3.0. - intervention_roi = (estimated_customer_ltv × intervention_success_probability × 0.7) − cost, rounded to 2 decimals; cost by recommended_intervention: Account Management Call=500; Executive Outreach=1000; Customer Success Check-in=200; Personalized Email Campaign=50; Product Adoption Workshop=300; Lifecycle-specific Campaign=100; otherwise=25. - risk_assessment_timestamp = current execution timestamp with time zone. - Final filter: include only rows with non-null primary_email. - Ordering: sort by critical_alert_flag (descending), then customer_priority_score (descending), potential_revenue_loss (descending), and total_risk_score (descending).'
