  marts_models:
    - name: customer360__address
      description: Consolidated customer addresses from Marketo and Stripe enriched with standardized country/state names and priority-based ranking
      grain: One row per sourced address per customer360_id (duplicates preserved)
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - staging.stg_customer360__country_codes
      - staging.stg_customer360__state_territory_codes
      business_logic: '- Read pass-through datasets: - marts.customer360__mapping as mapping (provides marketo_lead_id and stripe_customer_id per customer360_id) - staging.stg_customer360__country_codes as country_codes - staging.stg_customer360__state_territory_codes as state_codes - Build Marketo addresses (inner join mapping.marketo_lead_id = int_customer360__marketo.lead_id): - Primary address: include rows where address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "marketo", address_type = "primary", priority = 1; select address_line_1, address_line_2, city, state_code, country_code, postal_code - Billing address: include rows where billing_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "marketo", address_type = "billing", priority = 2; map billing_* fields to output columns - Build Stripe addresses (inner join mapping.stripe_customer_id = int_customer360__stripe.customer_id): - Customer address: include rows where customer_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "stripe", address_type = "customer", priority = 1; map customer_* fields - Shipping address: include rows where shipping_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "stripe", address_type = "shipping", priority = 2; map shipping_* fields - Union all Marketo and Stripe address rows; no de-duplication; only addresses with non-NULL address_line_1 are included. - Enrich with geographic names via left joins: - state: join state_codes on (state_code AND country_code) to derive state_territory; unmatched → NULL - country and country_alt_name: join country_codes on alpha-2 country code; unmatched → NULL - Compute rank: per customer360_id, assign row numbers ordered by priority ascending; within the same priority, order is unspecified and non-deterministic. - Output passes through source text as-is (casing/whitespace preserved); no normalization beyond the joins.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer key from mapping used to group and rank addresses; multiple rows per customer360_id
      - name: source_system
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Origin system literal ('marketo' or 'stripe'); set per source and always non-null
      - name: address_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Address category set per source: Marketo → ''primary'' or ''billing''; Stripe → ''customer'' or ''shipping'''
      - name: address_line_1
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary address line; rows are included only when this is non-null; text is passed through without trimming or case changes
      - name: address_line_2
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Secondary address line from source; may be null; text is passed through without trimming or case changes
      - name: city
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: City from source; may be null; no transformation
      - name: state_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: State/province code from source used for state name enrichment; may be null; case preserved
      - name: state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Resolved state/territory name from stg_customer360__state_territory_codes via (state_code,country_code) match; null if no match
      - name: country_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ISO alpha-2 country code from source used for joins; may be null; case preserved
      - name: country
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Resolved country name from stg_customer360__country_codes via country_code_alpha_2; null if no match
      - name: country_alt_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Alternative country name from stg_customer360__country_codes; null if no match
      - name: postal_code
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Postal code from source stored as BIGINT; may be null; numeric-only storage means leading zeros are not preserved
      - name: priority
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Address priority set by source (1 for primary/customer, 2 for billing/shipping); lower number indicates higher priority
      - name: rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Row number per customer360_id ordered by priority ascending; ties within the same priority have arbitrary order
    - name: customer360__conversion_funnel_analysis
      description: Conversion funnel metrics and optimization insights derived from behavior, lifecycle, and activity sources
      grain: One row per behavior_analysis record with non-null primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, primary_email, primary_organization, customer_first_touchpoint, customer_last_activity, customer_journey_pattern, customer_segment, marketing_to_sales_days, sales_to_support_days, account_age_days, in_marketo, in_stripe, in_zendesk, marketo_engagement, stripe_engagement, zendesk_engagement)
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (primary_email, lifecycle_stage, customer_health_score, estimated_customer_ltv, customer_tier)
      - marts.customer360__customer_activity_metrics (primary_email, activity_grade, weighted_engagement_score, primary_engagement_channel)
      business_logic: '- Begin with behavior_analysis and left join lifecycle_metrics and activity_metrics on primary_email. - Stage flags: reached_awareness = in_marketo; reached_conversion = in_stripe; reached_support = in_zendesk (1/0/NULL passthrough). - Speed buckets: awareness_to_conversion_speed from marketing_to_sales_days: ≤30 → Fast; ≤90 → Medium; ≤180 → Slow; >180 → Very Slow; missing → Direct to Sales. conversion_to_support_speed from sales_to_support_days: ≤7 → Immediate; ≤30 → Quick; ≤90 → Standard; >90 → Delayed; missing → No Support Needed. - journey_completeness_score: 3 if all three stage flags = 1; 2 if any two = 1; 1 if any one = 1; else 0. - Engagement quality passthrough: awareness_engagement_quality = marketo_engagement; conversion_engagement_quality = stripe_engagement; support_engagement_quality = zendesk_engagement. - funnel_efficiency: in_marketo = 1 and in_stripe = 1 and marketing_to_sales_days ≤ 60 → High Efficiency; same but ≤120 → Medium Efficiency; same (no day threshold) → Low Efficiency; in_stripe = 1 and in_marketo = 0 → Direct Conversion; else → No Conversion. - next_stage_conversion_probability (DECIMAL(3,2)): If reached_awareness = 1 and reached_conversion = 0: awareness_engagement_quality ≥ 4 and customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 → 0.85; ≥3 and ≥3.5 → 0.70; ≥2 and ≥3.0 → 0.55; ≥1 → 0.35; else → 0.15. Else if reached_conversion = 1 and reached_support = 0: conversion_engagement_quality ≥ 4 and customer_tier in {Platinum, Gold} → 0.75; ≥3 and customer_tier in {Gold, Silver} → 0.60; ≥2 → 0.45; else → 0.25. Else → 1.00. - value_realization_pattern: If reached_conversion = 1: estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 5000 and awareness_to_conversion_speed = Fast → Quick Value Realization; estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 2000 and awareness_to_conversion_speed in {Fast, Medium} → Standard Value Realization; awareness_to_conversion_speed in {Slow, Very Slow} → Delayed Value Realization; else → Unknown Value Timeline. Else → Pre-Value Stage. - drop_off_risk: reached_awareness = 1 and reached_conversion = 0 and account_age_days > 180 → High Drop-off Risk; reached_awareness = 1 and reached_conversion = 0 and awareness_engagement_quality ≤ 2 → Medium Drop-off Risk; reached_conversion = 1 and reached_support = 0 and conversion_engagement_quality ≤ 2 → Support Adoption Risk; else → Low Drop-off Risk. - journey_velocity: Use the sum of marketing_to_sales_days and sales_to_support_days, treating missing values as 0: completeness = 3 and sum ≤ 60 → Accelerated Journey; completeness ≥ 2 and sum ≤ 120 → Standard Journey; completeness ≥ 1 and sum ≤ 300 → Slow Journey; else → Stalled Journey. - cross_stage_engagement_consistency (DOUBLE, rounded to 2 decimals): If completeness ≥ 2: average of stage engagement scores where missing counts as 0 (sum divided by completeness). Else: use the single available score in order awareness, then conversion, then support; if none present use 0. - revenue_velocity_monthly (DOUBLE, rounded to 2 decimals): If reached_conversion = 1: monthly velocity = (estimated_customer_ltv ÷ days to sales), using 30 days when unavailable or less than 30, then ×30; else 0. Returns NULL if LTV is NULL. - optimization_recommendation: Awareness→Conversion is Slow/Very Slow and reached_conversion = 0 → if awareness_engagement_quality ≥ 3 then Accelerate Sales Qualification Process else Improve Marketing Lead Quality; Conversion→Support is Delayed and reached_support = 0 → Enhance Customer Success Onboarding; cross_stage_engagement_consistency < 2.5 → Implement Cross-Channel Coordination; journey_velocity = Stalled Journey → Reduce Funnel Friction Points; next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.7 → Accelerate High-Probability Conversions; drop_off_risk = High Drop-off Risk → Implement Retention Intervention; else → Standard Funnel Management. - expected_optimization_value (DECIMAL(18,2), rounded to 2 decimals): estimated_customer_ltv × (next_stage_conversion_probability − reduction) × tier_multiplier, where reduction = next_stage_conversion_probability × 0.7 if drop_off_risk is not Low Drop-off Risk else × 0.9, and tier_multiplier = 1.0 if LTV ≥ 5000, 0.8 if ≥2000, 0.6 if ≥1000, else 0.4. Returns NULL if LTV is NULL. - intervention_priority: next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.7 and estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 3000 → Critical Priority; next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.6 or estimated_customer_ltv ≥ 5000 → High Priority; next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.4 → Medium Priority; next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.2 → Low Priority; else → Monitor Only. - success_target: completeness = 3 → Maintain Full Journey Excellence; completeness = 2 and next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.6 → Complete Journey Progression; completeness = 1 and drop_off_risk = Low Drop-off Risk → Advance to Next Stage; drop_off_risk in {High Drop-off Risk, Medium Drop-off Risk} → Prevent Drop-off; else → Engage and Qualify. - funnel_performance_grade: completeness = 3 and journey_velocity = Accelerated Journey → A+; completeness = 3 and journey_velocity = Standard Journey → A; completeness = 2 and cross_stage_engagement_consistency ≥ 3.5 → B+; completeness = 2 and ≥ 3.0 → B; completeness = 1 and next_stage_conversion_probability ≥ 0.6 → C+; completeness = 1 and ≥ 0.4 → C; completeness = 1 → D; else → F. - journey_efficiency_index (DOUBLE, rounded to 2 decimals): 0.3 × completeness + 0.3 × velocity_score + 0.4 × cross_stage_engagement_consistency, where velocity_score = 5 for Accelerated Journey, 4 for Standard Journey, 2 for Slow Journey, else 1. - predictive_full_journey_probability (DOUBLE, rounded to 3 decimals): 0.4 × next_stage_conversion_probability + 0.3 × drop_off_weight + 0.3 × (cross_stage_engagement_consistency ÷ 5.0), where drop_off_weight = 0.9 for Low Drop-off Risk, 0.7 for Support Adoption Risk, 0.5 for Medium Drop-off Risk, else 0.2. - funnel_analysis_timestamp: set to the current system timestamp (time zone aware). - Final selection and ordering: include only records with a present primary_email; order by intervention_priority (descending lexicographic), then expected_optimization_value (descending), journey_efficiency_index (descending), predictive_full_journey_probability (descending).'

      - name: funnel_efficiency

      - name: sales_to_support_days

      - name: conversion_to_support_speed

        description: 'Speed bucket from sales_to_support_days: Immediate≤7, Quick≤30, Standard≤90, Delayed>90, or No Support Needed if NULL'
      - name: journey_velocity
        data_type: VARCHAR

      - name: awareness_engagement_quality

      - name: conversion_engagement_quality

        description: Conversion-stage engagement score from behavior_analysis; may be NULL
      - name: support_engagement_quality

      - name: cross_stage_engagement_consistency

      - name: predictive_full_journey_probability

      - name: drop_off_risk

      - name: value_realization_pattern

      - name: optimization_recommendation

      - name: estimated_customer_ltv

      - name: account_age_days

      - name: customer_first_touchpoint

      - name: customer_last_activity

    - name: customer360__customer
      description: Unified customer and organization header profile with pass-through attributes and deterministic sample metrics/aggregations.
      grain: One row per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - marts.customer360__summary
      business_logic: '1) Build a dimensions set by inner joining marts.customer360__mapping to marts.customer360__summary on customer360_id, selecting: customer360_organization_id, is_organization_header, source_ids (from mapping) and email, full_name, organization_name, address_line_1, address_line_2, city, state, country, country_alt_name, postal_code, ip_address, phone (from summary). Only ids present in both sources are kept; all fields are passed through as stored. 2) For non-organization headers (is_organization_header = FALSE), assign sample metrics per customer360_id: - For ''sample_customer_1'': sends=10, opens=3, clicks=1, sales_amount=1250.00, sales_count=2, first_sale_date=2024-01-15, most_recent_sale_date=2024-03-15, tickets_created=3, tickets_resolved=2, avg_satisfaction=4.5. - For all others: sends=5, opens=2, clicks=0, sales_amount=750.00, sales_count=1, first_sale_date=2024-02-10, most_recent_sale_date=2024-02-10, tickets_created=1, tickets_resolved=1, avg_satisfaction=5.0. 3) Combine dimensions with these metrics by customer360_id. For rows without assigned metrics (headers), set numeric metrics to 0 (including avg_satisfaction_score) and leave first_sale_date and most_recent_sale_date as NULL. 4) For organization headers only, produce one row per unique header by aggregating the combined dataset across the header’s own rows: sum email sends/opens/clicks, sum sales amount and sales count, take the earliest first_sale_date, the latest most_recent_sale_date, sum tickets created/resolved, and average the satisfaction score. Aggregations consider only header rows (child/customer rows are not included in header rollups); standard null handling applies to aggregates (nulls are ignored in averages; earliest/latest dates return NULL if all inputs are NULL). 5) Output includes all non-header rows from step 3 and the aggregated header rows from step 4 appended together. No specific output ordering is enforced.'
      columns:

        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary identifier; one output row per id; also the join key between mapping and summary.
      - name: customer360_organization_id
        data_type: VARCHAR

      - name: is_organization_header

      - name: email

        description: Email from summary; passed through.
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from summary; passed through.
      - name: organization_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name from summary; passed through.
      - name: address_line_1
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Address line 1 from summary; passed through.
      - name: address_line_2
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Address line 2 from summary; passed through.
      - name: city
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: City from summary; passed through.
      - name: state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: State/region from summary; passed through.
      - name: country
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Country from summary; passed through.
      - name: country_alt_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Alternative country name from summary; passed through.
      - name: postal_code
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Postal/ZIP code from summary stored as numeric; passed through.
      - name: ip_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: IP address from summary; passed through.
      - name: phone
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Phone number from summary; passed through.
      - name: marketing_email_sends
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 'Count of marketing emails sent; non-headers: 10 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 5; headers: summed across header rows; missing metrics default to 0.'
      - name: marketing_email_opens
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 'Count of marketing email opens; non-headers: 3 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 2; headers: summed across header rows; missing metrics default to 0.'
      - name: marketing_email_clicks
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 'Count of marketing email clicks; non-headers: 1 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 0; headers: summed across header rows; missing metrics default to 0.'
      - name: total_sales_amount
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: 'Total sales amount; non-headers: 1250.00 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 750.00; headers: summed across header rows; missing metrics default to 0.00.'
      - name: total_sales_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 'Total number of sales; non-headers: 2 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 1; headers: summed across header rows; missing metrics default to 0.'
      - name: first_sale_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: 'First sale date; non-headers: 2024-01-15 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 2024-02-10; headers: earliest across header rows; NULL if no non-NULL values.'
      - name: most_recent_sale_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: 'Most recent sale date; non-headers: 2024-03-15 for ''sample_customer_1'' else 2024-02-10; headers: latest across header rows; NULL if no non-NULL values.'
      - name: support_tickets_created

    - name: customer360__customer_activity_metrics
      description: Customer activity and engagement metrics across marketing, sales, and support with recency, velocity, depth, risk, and intervention signals
      grain: One row per primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: 'Overview - Start from behavior_analysis (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis, one row per customer) and left join lifecycle_metrics (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) on primary_email. - Enrich with platform data via left joins on platform IDs: - Marketo: intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on lead_id - Stripe: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on customer_id - Zendesk: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on user_id - Filter: exclude rows where primary_email is NULL; no de-duplication beyond joins. - Time anchors: current_date for recency calculations and current_timestamp for activity_analysis_timestamp; results vary by execution time. - Ordering: rows are sorted by activity_priority_score (desc), then weighted_engagement_score (desc), then active_channel_count (desc). Activity recency and counts - days/weeks/months_since_last_activity: difference between customer_last_activity and current_date by unit; returns NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL. - active_channel_count: integer sum (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); if any flag is NULL the sum becomes NULL; expected domain is 0–3 from 0/1 flags. Estimated and adjusted activity (stochastic components) - estimated_monthly_activities: simulated with random() per run based on composite_engagement_score: - >=4.0 → 15 + floor(random()*10) ∈ [15,24] - >=3.0 → 8 + floor(random()*7) ∈ [8,14] - >=2.0 → 3 + floor(random()*5) ∈ [3,7] - >=1.0 → 1 + floor(random()*3) ∈ [1,3] - else → floor(random()*2) ∈ [0,1] - Note: random() yields different results each execution; this column is non-deterministic by design. - seasonally_adjusted_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a month factor (Nov/Dec/Jan ×1.2; Jun/Jul/Aug ×0.8; else ×1.0); no rounding. - predicted_next_month_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a factor from engagement_velocity category (Accelerating ×1.3; Steady High ×1.1; Steady Medium ×1.0; Declining ×0.7; Slow ×0.4; Stagnant ×0.2); no rounding. Engagement velocity, momentum, maturity (rule-based categories) - engagement_velocity (uses activity recency and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.0 → Accelerating - <=14 days and score>=2.5 → Steady High - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Steady Medium - <=60 days → Declining - <=90 days → Slow - else → Stagnant - activity_momentum (uses days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.5 → High Momentum - <=14 days and score>=3.0 → Medium Momentum - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Low Momentum - <=60 days → Losing Momentum - else → No Momentum - engagement_maturity (uses account_age_days and active_channel_count): - age>=365 and channels>=3 → Mature Multi-channel - age>=180 and channels>=2 → Developing Multi-channel - age>=90 and channels>=1 → Single Channel Engaged - age<90 → Early Stage - else → Minimal Engagement Channel scores and depths - marketing_engagement_score: if in_marketo=1 and is_unsubscribed=false and is_email_invalid=false then round(marketo_engagement × (1 − days since last Marketo update / 90), 2); else 0; may be negative; if the last update timestamp is NULL the result is NULL in the true branch. - sales_engagement_score: if in_stripe=1 and is_deleted=false and is_delinquent=false then round(stripe_engagement × (1 − days since last Stripe update / 60), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - support_engagement_score: if in_zendesk=1 and is_active=true and is_suspended=false and is_deleted=false then round(zendesk_engagement × (1 − days since last Zendesk update / 120), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - primary_engagement_channel: choose the channel with the highest raw engagement; ties break in order Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced. - marketing_depth/sales_depth/support_depth (per channel): if in_* = 1: engagement>=4 → Deep; engagement>=2 → Medium; else → Shallow; if in_*=0 → None. Cross-platform and composite scores - cross_platform_consistency: round( average of raw engagement across platforms where in_*=1, 2 decimals ); returns NULL if no active platforms or if any included operand (flags or raw engagements) is NULL. - activity_efficiency: round(composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count, 2); NULL if active_channel_count is 0 or NULL. - weighted_engagement_score: round(0.3×marketing_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.5×sales_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.2×support_engagement_score (NULL→0), 2); can be negative. - activity_grade: from weighted_engagement_score and active_channel_count: >=4.0 & channels>=3 → A+; >=3.5 & channels>=2 → A; >=3.0 → B+; >=2.5 → B; >=2.0 → C+; >=1.5 → C; >=1.0 → D; else → F. - activity_priority_score: round(0.4×weighted_engagement_score + 0.3×active_channel_count + 0.3×priority_component, 2) where priority_component is 5/4/3/2/1 by recency+composite rules (<=7 days & score>=3.5 → 5; <=14 & score>=3.0 → 4; <=30 & score>=2.0 → 3; <=60 → 2; else → 1). Risk and interventions - activity_risk_level: if days_since_last_activity>90 and customer_health_score<3.0 → High Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>60 or active_channel_count=1 → Medium Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>30 → Low Activity Risk; else → No Activity Risk. - recommended_activity_intervention (evaluated top-to-bottom): Declining/Slow/Stagnant with health>=3.0 → Re-engagement Campaign; else single channel (count=1) with composite>=2.5 → Channel Expansion; else Marketing Driven with in_stripe=0 → Sales Conversion Focus; else Sales Driven with in_zendesk=0 → Success Onboarding; else recent (<=7 days) with composite>=3.5 → Upsell Opportunity; else Standard Engagement.'
      columns:
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: primary_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer email key; rows with NULL are excluded from output; grain is one row per primary_email
      - name: primary_organization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer organization from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer segment from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: customer_journey_pattern
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Journey pattern label from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: lifecycle_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lifecycle stage from lifecycle_metrics joined on primary_email; may be NULL
      - name: composite_engagement_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Base composite engagement score from behavior_analysis; used by multiple downstream rules without further rounding
      - name: weighted_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 0.3*marketing_engagement_score + 0.5*sales_engagement_score + 0.2*support_engagement_score rounded to 2 decimals; NULL channel scores treated as 0; may be negative
      - name: customer_health_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(15,2)
        description: Health score from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough value used in risk and intervention logic
      - name: activity_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Letter grade from weighted_engagement_score and active_channel_count with thresholds: A+, A, B+, B, C+, C, D, F as defined in Business Logic'
      - name: activity_priority_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Priority score rounded to 2 decimals: 0.4*weighted_engagement_score + 0.3*active_channel_count + 0.3*recency_component (5–1) per rules'
      - name: days_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of days between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: weeks_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of weeks between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: months_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of months between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: account_age_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Account age in days from behavior_analysis; passthrough value used in maturity logic
      - name: active_channel_count
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Sum of in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk (expected 0–3); NULL if any flag is NULL
      - name: primary_engagement_channel
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Channel with highest raw engagement; ties break Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; fallback Balanced when comparisons cannot be resolved (e.g., NULL inputs)
      - name: marketing_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_marketo=1 and not unsubscribed/invalid then mark_engagement×(1 − days since last update/90) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: sales_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_stripe=1 and not deleted and not delinquent then stripe_engagement×(1 − days since last update/60) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: support_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_zendesk=1 and active and not suspended/deleted then zendesk_engagement×(1 − days since last update/120) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: marketing_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Marketo: if in_marketo=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_marketo=0 then None'
      - name: sales_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Stripe: if in_stripe=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_stripe=0 then None'
      - name: support_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Zendesk: if in_zendesk=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_zendesk=0 then None'
      - name: engagement_velocity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Velocity category from recency and composite_engagement_score: Accelerating, Steady High, Steady Medium, Declining, Slow, or Stagnant per thresholds'
      - name: activity_momentum
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Momentum category from days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score: High/Medium/Low Momentum, Losing Momentum, or No Momentum per thresholds'
      - name: engagement_maturity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Maturity category from account_age_days and active_channel_count: Mature Multi-channel, Developing Multi-channel, Single Channel Engaged, Early Stage, or Minimal Engagement'
      - name: estimated_monthly_activities
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Simulated integer in defined ranges using random() and composite_engagement_score; stochastic and varies each run
      - name: predicted_next_month_activity
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Estimated future activity = estimated_monthly_activities × factor from engagement_velocity (1.3/1.1/1.0/0.7/0.4/0.2); not rounded
      - name: seasonally_adjusted_activity
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Estimated_monthly_activities adjusted by month: Nov–Jan ×1.2, Jun–Aug ×0.8, else ×1.0; not rounded'
      - name: active_30_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 30 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_60_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 60 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_90_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 90 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_180_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 180 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_365_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 365 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: activity_risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk category from days_since_last_activity, customer_health_score, and active_channel_count: High/Medium/Low/No Activity Risk per rules'
      - name: cross_platform_consistency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of raw engagement across active platforms (in_*=1) rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if no active platforms or any included operand is NULL
      - name: activity_efficiency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if denominator is 0 or NULL
      - name: recommended_activity_intervention
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Intervention label evaluated in order: Re-engagement Campaign, Channel Expansion, Sales Conversion Focus, Success Onboarding, Upsell Opportunity, else Standard Engagement'
      - name: in_marketo
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL
      - name: in_stripe
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL
      - name: in_zendesk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL

      - name: do_not_call

      - name: is_delinquent

      - name: stripe_deleted

      - name: zendesk_active

      - name: zendesk_suspended

      - name: zendesk_deleted

        description: Zendesk deletion flag from platform data; must be false for support_engagement_score to be computed
      - name: customer_first_touchpoint

      - name: customer_last_activity

      - name: marketo_registration_date

      - name: stripe_registration_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Stripe created_at from platform data; passthrough
      - name: zendesk_registration_date

      - name: activity_analysis_timestamp

    - name: customer360__customer_value_analysis
      description: Customer value analysis with RFM, adjusted LTV, portfolio metrics, risk and engagement recommendations
      grain: One row per customer (from int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) with non-null primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (aliased lm), compute RFM metrics and value segments, then portfolio and recommendation metrics; finally filter to rows where primary_email is not NULL and sort for presentation (sorting does not affect metric values). - Monetary score: bucket lm.estimated_customer_value into {>=5000→5, >=3000→4, >=1500→3, >=800→2, else 1}. - RFM score string: concatenate recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score with no delimiter in R-F-M order; if any component is NULL the result is NULL. - RFM average: average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score, rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL. - RFM segment: apply deterministic rules in this order: rfm_avg_score≥4.5→Champions; rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and recency_score≥4→Loyal Customers; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥4→Potential Loyalists; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→New Customers; recency_score≥3 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≤2→Promising; recency_score≥3 and monetary_score≥3→Customers Needing Attention; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≥3→At Risk; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≥4→Cannot Lose Them; recency_score≤1 and frequency_score≥2→Hibernating; else Lost. - Adjusted LTV: estimated_customer_ltv multiplied by lifecycle_stage multiplier {Acquisition 0.3, Activation 0.6, Growth 1.2, Maturity 1.0, Retention 0.8, else 0.5}; not explicitly rounded; stored with 3-decimal precision. - Revenue tier: by estimated_customer_ltv thresholds {≥10000 Tier 1 - Strategic; ≥5000 Tier 2 - High Value; ≥2500 Tier 3 - Core; ≥1000 Tier 4 - Developing; else Tier 5 - Basic}. - Value stability: by customer_health_score and churn_probability {≥4.0 and ≤0.20→High Stability; ≥3.0 and ≤0.40→Medium Stability; ≥2.0 and ≤0.60→Low Stability; else Unstable}. - Upsell potential: {rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and frequency_score≥4→High Upsell; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥3→Medium Upsell; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→Cross-sell Focus; else Retention Focus}. - Expected annual revenue: compute adjusted_ltv × (1 − churn_probability) divided by the age denominator (account_age_days/365.0 when account_age_days≥365, otherwise 1); round to 2 decimals; returns NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL. - Portfolio contribution pct: adjusted_ltv divided by the total adjusted_ltv across all customers in the portfolio (computed before the final email filter), multiplied by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when the portfolio total is 0 or NULL. - Concentration risk: by adjusted_ltv {≥50000→High Concentration Risk; ≥20000→Medium Concentration Risk; else Low Concentration Risk}. - Investment priority score: weighted composite of rfm_segment (40%), revenue_tier (30%), and churn risk (30%), rounded to 2 decimals; segment weights {Champions 5; Loyal Customers 4.5; Potential Loyalists 4; New Customers 3.5; Promising 3; Customers Needing Attention 4.5; At Risk 5; Cannot Lose Them 5; Hibernating 2; else 1}; revenue tier weights {Tier 1 - Strategic 5; Tier 2 - High Value 4; Tier 3 - Core 3; Tier 4 - Developing 2; else 1}; churn risk weights by churn_probability {≥0.70→5; ≥0.50→4; ≥0.30→3; ≥0.10→2; else 1}. - Acquisition ROI assessment: by expected_annual_revenue {≥5000→Excellent ROI; ≥2000→Good ROI; ≥1000→Acceptable ROI; ≥500→Marginal ROI; else→Poor ROI}. - Strategic classification: combine rfm_segment and revenue_tier: {(Champions, Cannot Lose Them)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Strategic Account; (Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists)∧(Tier 2, Tier 3)→Key Account; (New Customers, Promising)∧(Tier 3, Tier 4)→Growth Account; (At Risk, Hibernating)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Recovery Account; else→Standard Account}. - Recommended engagement model: map strategic_classification {Strategic→Executive Relationship Management; Key→Dedicated Account Management; Growth→Expansion Programs; Recovery→Retention & Recovery Initiatives; else→Standard Engagement}. - Investment recommendation: by investment_priority_score {≥4.5→High Investment; ≥3.5→Medium Investment; ≥2.5→Standard Investment; else→Minimal Investment}. - Success target: by rfm_segment {Champions/Loyal Customers→Maintain Excellence; Potential Loyalists/Customers Needing Attention→Drive Engagement; New Customers/Promising→Accelerate Onboarding; At Risk/Cannot Lose Them→Immediate Intervention; else→Reactivation Required}. - Revenue risk percentage: churn_probability expressed as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv is NULL or zero. - Development opportunity: by upsell_potential and value_stability {High Upsell∧High Stability→Premium Growth; High/Medium Upsell→Expansion Ready; Cross-sell Focus→Product Adoption; else→Value Preservation}. - Analysis timestamp: set at query execution time (time zone preserved). - Final filter and ordering: keep only rows with primary_email IS NOT NULL; order by investment_priority_score desc, adjusted_ltv desc, customer_health_score desc.'
      columns:
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead identifier from lifecycle metrics; may be NULL if not available
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer identifier from lifecycle metrics; opaque string; may be NULL
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user identifier from lifecycle metrics; may be NULL
      - name: primary_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary customer email; final result filters to non-NULL values
      - name: primary_organization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer organization name from lifecycle metrics; free text; may be NULL
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Upstream segment label from lifecycle metrics; not recomputed here
      - name: customer_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Upstream customer tier from lifecycle metrics; not recomputed here
      - name: rfm_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic RFM segment per case rules using rfm_avg_score, recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score
      - name: rfm_score
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Three-digit string formed by concatenating recency, frequency, and monetary scores in R-F-M order with no delimiter; NULL if any component is NULL
      - name: rfm_avg_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL
      - name: recency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Recency score from lifecycle metrics (expected 1–5); higher is more recent; may be NULL
      - name: frequency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Frequency score from lifecycle metrics (expected 1–5); higher is more frequent; may be NULL
      - name: monetary_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Derived spend score (1–5) bucketed from estimated_customer_value using thresholds: >=5000, >=3000, >=1500, >=800, else 1'
      - name: estimated_customer_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
        description: Upstream estimated customer lifetime value in source currency with 2-decimal precision; may be NULL
      - name: adjusted_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,3)
        description: 'Lifecycle-stage-adjusted LTV (multipliers: Acquisition 0.3, Activation 0.6, Growth 1.2, Maturity 1.0, Retention 0.8, else 0.5) stored with 3-decimal precision; not explicitly rounded in SQL'
      - name: expected_annual_revenue
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Adjusted LTV × (1 − churn_probability) divided by account_age_days/365.0 when age≥365, otherwise by 1; rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL
      - name: revenue_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier based on estimated_customer_ltv: >=10000 Tier 1 - Strategic; >=5000 Tier 2 - High Value; >=2500 Tier 3 - Core; >=1000 Tier 4 - Developing; else Tier 5 - Basic'
      - name: strategic_classification
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Account class from rfm_segment and revenue_tier: Strategic, Key, Growth, Recovery, or Standard per deterministic mapping'
      - name: value_stability
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Stability category by customer_health_score and churn_probability: High, Medium, Low, or Unstable per thresholds'
      - name: upsell_potential
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Opportunity label from RFM metrics: High Upsell, Medium Upsell, Cross-sell Focus, or Retention Focus'
      - name: churn_probability
        data_type: DECIMAL(3,2)
        description: Probability of churn in [0.00,1.00] from lifecycle metrics; used directly in downstream formulas
      - name: potential_revenue_loss
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
        description: Product of adjusted LTV and churn_probability rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if either input is NULL
      - name: revenue_risk_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Churn probability expressed as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv is NULL or zero
      - name: portfolio_contribution_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Adjusted LTV as a percentage of total adjusted LTV across all customers (before email filter), rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when the portfolio total is 0 or NULL
      - name: concentration_risk
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk bucket by adjusted_ltv: >=50000 High, >=20000 Medium, else Low Concentration Risk'
      - name: investment_priority_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(15,2)
        description: Weighted composite of segment (40%), revenue tier (30%), and churn risk (30%), rounded to 2 decimals
      - name: acquisition_roi_assessment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'ROI category by expected_annual_revenue: Excellent, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Poor ROI'
      - name: recommended_engagement_model
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Engagement model derived from strategic_classification: Executive, Dedicated AM, Expansion Programs, Retention & Recovery, or Standard'
      - name: investment_recommendation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Allocation suggestion by investment_priority_score: High, Medium, Standard, or Minimal Investment'
      - name: success_target
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Customer success focus by rfm_segment: Maintain Excellence, Drive Engagement, Accelerate Onboarding, Immediate Intervention, or Reactivation Required'
      - name: development_opportunity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Opportunity theme by upsell_potential and value_stability: Premium Growth, Expansion Ready, Product Adoption, or Value Preservation'
      - name: customer_health_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(15,2)
        description: Upstream health score (higher is better) used in stability scoring; 2-decimal precision
      - name: lifecycle_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer lifecycle stage from lifecycle metrics (e.g., Acquisition, Activation, Growth, Maturity, Retention)
      - name: risk_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk bucket by churn_probability: >=0.70 High Risk; >=0.50 Medium Risk; >=0.30 Low Risk; else Minimal Risk'
      - name: account_age_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Age of account in days from lifecycle metrics; used to normalize expected_annual_revenue
      - name: days_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days since the last activity from lifecycle metrics; passthrough field
      - name: analysis_timestamp

    - name: customer360__email
      description: Unique customer emails per customer360_id with a deterministic 1-based index ordered by email ascending
      grain: One row per unique (customer360_id, email)
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read customer-to-system ID links from marts.customer360__mapping (uses: customer360_id, marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id). - Collect emails from each source via inner joins to mapping: - Marketo: mapping.marketo_lead_id = marketo.lead_id - Stripe: mapping.stripe_customer_id = stripe.customer_id - Zendesk: mapping.zendesk_user_id = zendesk.user_id - Exclude rows where the source email is NULL; preserve original casing and spacing; do not trim or normalize. - Union all collected rows across sources. - De-duplicate to a unique set of (customer360_id, email) using exact string equality. - For each customer360_id, sort emails ascending by their literal value (default lexicographic order) and assign a contiguous 1-based sequential index; output customer360_id, email, and index. - If a customer has no non-NULL emails in any source, no row is emitted for that customer.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 ID from mapping; groups emails and defines the partition for indexing; no explicit NULL filtering
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email from Marketo/Stripe/Zendesk via mapping joins; NULLs excluded; duplicates removed by exact string equality; casing and whitespace preserved without normalization
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Contiguous 1-based sequential index within each customer360_id after sorting emails ascending; stable given the same deduplicated email set
    - name: customer360__ip_address
      description: Latest Marketo IP address per customer360_id based on updated_at
      grain: One row per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping (customer360_id, marketo_lead_id)
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo (lead_id, ip_address, updated_at)
      business_logic: '- Build the customer-to-Marketo mapping from marts.customer360__mapping (customer360_id ↔ marketo_lead_id). - Join to intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on marketo_lead_id = lead_id. - Exclude rows where ip_address is NULL; customers without any non-NULL IP do not appear in the output. - For each customer360_id, sort candidate rows by updated_at descending and assign a rank starting at 1. - Select the single row with rank = 1 per customer360_id: - This corresponds to the most recent updated_at for that customer. - If multiple rows share the same updated_at, the chosen row is unspecified because no tie-breaker is defined. - NULL placement in sorting uses the database default; if all updated_at are NULL for a customer, one NULL row is chosen arbitrarily. - Output columns come from the selected row: customer360_id (from mapping), ip_address (from Marketo), source_system (constant ''marketo''), last_seen (Marketo updated_at).'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 identifier used to group rows and select the most recent Marketo IP
      - name: ip_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: IP address from the chosen Marketo row; preserved as stored; never NULL due to filtering; selection in update-time ties is arbitrary
      - name: source_system
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant 'marketo' for all rows
      - name: last_seen
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: updated_at from the chosen Marketo row (the most recent per customer360_id; tie and NULL ordering follow the database default)
    - name: customer360__mapping
      description: Customer identity mapping linking unified and organizational hashes to source system records and an organization-level header row with aggregated metadata
      grain: 'Mixed: individual rows per combined source record (is_organization_header=false) and one header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true)'
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '1) Load four inputs: source_matches, marketo, stripe, zendesk. 2) Build combine_all_results: - Chain full outer joins: source_matches to marketo on lead_id, then to stripe on customer_id from source_matches, then to zendesk on user_id from source_matches, retaining all records from every source. - For IDs, prefer the value from source_matches when present; otherwise use the corresponding source table value. - Per-row timestamps: - marketo_updated_at = the most recent non-null updated_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - marketo_created_at = the earliest non-null created_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - stripe_updated_at / stripe_created_at = the stripe timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from stripe. - zendesk_updated_at / zendesk_created_at = the zendesk timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk. - zendesk_organization_* = the zendesk organization timestamps from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk.organization_*. - Union in three additional sets to also include any marketo/stripe/zendesk records whose IDs are not present in source_matches; these rows carry only their own system fields, others null. This can yield duplicates relative to the full outer joins. 3) For each row, derive customer360_organization_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo org name without suffix, marketo inferred org name without suffix, stripe customer org name without suffix, stripe shipping org name without suffix, zendesk organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings. 4) Emit two row types: - Individual rows (is_organization_header=false): include the three source IDs; source_ids is a compact JSON-like object {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} where null IDs are rendered as empty strings; timestamps are the per-row values from step 2. - One organization header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true): source IDs are null; source_ids is a JSON-like object with arrays per system containing distinct quoted IDs for that organization (comma-delimited, no spaces), with nulls rendered as empty strings; timestamps aggregated per organization as latest updated_at and earliest created_at for each system; zendesk organization timestamps use latest for updated and earliest for created. 5) Assign customer360_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, is_organization_header, customer360_organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings and using the engine’s string form of the boolean.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_lead_id|stripe_customer_id|zendesk_user_id|is_organization_header|customer360_organization_id with nulls as empty strings and the engine’s string form of the boolean.
      - name: customer360_organization_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_org_name_no_suffix|marketo_inferred_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_customer_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_shipping_org_name_no_suffix|zendesk_organization_id with nulls as empty strings.
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else marketo; null on organization header rows.
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else stripe; null on organization header rows.
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else zendesk; null on organization header rows.
      - name: is_organization_header
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: 'Row type flag: false for individual rows; true for the single aggregated header row per customer360_organization_id.'
      - name: source_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'JSON-like string; individual rows: {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} with nulls as empty strings; header rows: arrays per system of distinct quoted IDs joined by commas (no spaces), nulls as empty strings, order not enforced.'
      - name: marketo_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: latest non-null updated_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: latest marketo_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: marketo_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: earliest non-null created_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: earliest marketo_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: latest stripe_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: earliest stripe_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest zendesk_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest org updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest zendesk_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest org created_at in the organization; null if none.'
    - name: customer360__name
      description: Deduplicated customer full names from Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk with lexicographic variant indexing per customer360_id
      grain: One row per unique full_name per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Start from marts.customer360__mapping to relate customer360_id to source system identifiers. - Collect name candidates via inner joins, excluding rows where the source name is NULL: - Marketo: join by lead ID; use full_name_clean. - Stripe (customer): join by customer ID; use customer_name_clean. - Stripe (shipping): join by customer ID; use shipping_name_clean. - Zendesk: join by user ID; use full_name_clean. - Union all candidates from all sources; any temporary source or index flags used during collection are ignored. - Deduplicate to unique (customer360_id, full_name) pairs; duplicates within a customer are removed, across customers are preserved. - For each customer360_id, sort remaining full_name values in ascending lexicographic order under the database’s default collation and assign a sequential index starting at 1. - Output columns: customer360_id, full_name, index.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer key; one row per unique full_name within each customer360_id.
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name taken as-is from upstream cleaned fields; NULLs are excluded, empty strings may appear; deduplicated per customer360_id; the exact string determines ordering for index.
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Sequential position within each customer360_id after deduplication, starting at 1 and ordered by full_name ascending; consecutive integers with no gaps; not based on source priority.
    - name: customer360__organization
      description: Distinct organization names per customer360_id, alphabetically indexed after consolidating Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk sources
      grain: One row per distinct organization_name per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read marts.customer360__mapping to obtain customer360_id and source identifiers: - marketo_lead_id → intermediate.int_customer360__marketo.lead_id - stripe_customer_id → intermediate.int_customer360__stripe.customer_id - zendesk_user_id → intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk.user_id - Collect organization names via inner joins; exclude rows where the selected name is NULL: - Marketo: organization_name_no_suffix; Marketo inferred: inferred_organization_name_no_suffix - Stripe: customer_organization_name_no_suffix; Stripe shipping: shipping_organization_name_no_suffix - Zendesk: organization_name - Union all collected names across sources. - Deduplicate by exact string equality on (customer360_id, organization_name); casing and whitespace are preserved (no trimming or normalization). - Assign final index as the alphabetical position per customer360_id by ordering organization_name ascending using the database’s default collation; indices start at 1 and are contiguous. - Output customer360_id, organization_name, index.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 identifier from mapping used to group and index organizations; never NULL due to inner joins
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: organization_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Organization name from Marketo (no_suffix or inferred no_suffix), Stripe (customer or shipping no_suffix), or Zendesk; NULL names are excluded; duplicates removed per customer360_id by exact string match; original casing and spacing kept; used for alphabetical indexing
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Alphabetical rank within the deduplicated organization_name list for the customer360_id; starts at 1, contiguous, ordered by organization_name ascending; unrelated to any source-specific priority
        tests:
        - not_null
    - name: customer360__organization_network
      description: Organization-level network, value, health, engagement, risk, ranking, and strategy metrics grouped by standardized_org_name + email_domain (INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER excluded)
      grain: One row per (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      - marts.customer360__customer_value_analysis
      business_logic: '- Build organization_entities: - Join behavior_analysis to lifecycle_metrics on primary_email; join behavior_analysis to value_analysis on primary_email. - Retain ids (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id), journey/segment fields, LTV/health/engagement fields. - Standardize fields: - standardized_org_name: uppercase and trim primary_organization; if null/blank set "INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER". - email_domain: take the substring after "@" in primary_email; if missing set "unknown.domain". - organization_type by primary_organization text patterns: - null/blank → Individual - contains inc/corp/llc/ltd → Corporation - contains university/college/school → Education - contains government/dept/agency → Government - contains nonprofit/foundation/charity → Non-Profit - otherwise → Business - estimated_org_size: - domain in {gmail.com,yahoo.com,hotmail.com,outlook.com} → Personal - domain in {microsoft.com,google.com,amazon.com,apple.com,facebook.com} → Enterprise - else if name length > 20 → Large Business; > 10 → Medium Business; > 0 → Small Business; otherwise → Individual - Aggregate to organization_aggregates at (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size): - Counts (distinct primary_email): total_contacts; marketing_contacts when marketo_lead_id present; sales_contacts when stripe_customer_id present; support_contacts when zendesk_user_id present. - Journey distribution: full_journey_contacts when journey pattern = "Full Journey"; also compute marketing_to_sales_contacts and sales_to_support_contacts (used downstream). - Value metrics: total_organization_ltv (sum of estimated_customer_ltv), avg_customer_ltv, highest_customer_ltv (max), total_adjusted_ltv (sum). - Engagement/health: avg_engagement_score (average composite_engagement_score), max_engagement_score (max), avg_health_score (average customer_health_score). - Strategic classification: strategic_accounts, key_accounts, growth_accounts, recovery_accounts from strategic_classification. - Revenue tiers: tier1_contacts, tier2_contacts, tier3_contacts from revenue_tier. - Customer segments: champions, loyal_customers, at_risk_customers from customer_segment. - Lifecycle stages (for health calc): growth_stage_contacts when stage = "Growth"; ≥25000→4; ≥10000→3; ≥5000→2; else→1 (weight 0.4). - Contacts tier: ≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥3→3; ≥2→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - Avg engagement tier: ≥4.0→5; ≥3.0→4; ≥2.5→3; ≥2.0→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - organization_health_score: 0.4×avg_health_score + 0.3×(champions+loyal_customers)/total_contacts×5 + 0.3×(growth_stage_contacts+maturity_stage_contacts)/total_contacts×5; if total_contacts=0, both ratios are 0; round to two decimals. - account_penetration_score: share of contacts linked across marketing, sales, and support out of three touchpoints, scaled to a 0–5 score and rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0. - concentration_risk: - if total_contacts=1 → High Concentration Risk - else if total_contacts≤3 → Medium Concentration Risk - else if email_domains_count=1 and total_contacts≥5 → Domain Concentration Risk - else → Low Concentration Risk - Perform network_analysis: - market_share_within_type: percent share of total_organization_ltv within the same organization_type, rounded to four decimals; else if total_contacts≥2 and support_contacts=0 →2; else →0. - Growth: High Growth Potential →2; Medium Growth Potential →1; else →0. - Engagement: avg_engagement_score≥3.5 →2; ≥3.0 →1; else →0. - expansion_priority: - if strategic_value_tier in {Strategic Enterprise, Key Enterprise} and growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Immediate Expansion - else if organization_value_score≥4.0 and organization_health_score≥4.0 → High Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥3 and avg_engagement_score≥3.0 → Medium Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥2 and organization_risk_level=Stable → Low Priority Expansion - else → Maintenance Mode - recommended_strategy: - if organization_risk_level=High Risk → Risk Mitigation & Recovery - else if strategic_value_tier=Strategic Enterprise → White Glove Account Management - else if strategic_value_tier=Key Enterprise → Dedicated Account Management - else if growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Growth & Expansion Focus - else if total_contacts=1 → Relationship Expansion - else → Standard Account Management - Finalization: - organization_influence_score: weighted score rounded to two decimals = 0.3×organization_value_score + 0.3×contacts tier (≥10→5; staging_contract:

  quality_actions:

      examples: ["LOWER(TRIM(email))", "standardize timezone formats", "normalize phone numbers"]
    
    delete_row:
      description: "Remove entire row when records contain severe data quality issues that make them unusable downstream."
      examples: ["Explicitly marked for deletion", "Confirmed duplicates", "Invalid primary keys", "Essential business attributes contain irrecoverable errors"]
    
    nullify_field:
      description: "Set invalid field values to NULL when the field is non-critical and record can still be useful"
      examples: ["malformed optional URLs", "invalid secondary contact information", "corrupted metadata fields"]

  tables:
    # Reference Data Tables
    - name: stg_customer360__country_codes
      description: "Standardized country code reference data supporting ISO 3166 standards for geographic data validation and normalization"
      source_table: raw.country_codes
      columns:
        - name: country_name

          constraints: [not_null]

            - rule: "LENGTH(TRIM(country_name)) > 0"

        - name: alternative_country_name

        - name: country_code_numeric
          data_type: INTEGER
          validation_rules:

        - name: country_code_alpha_2

            - rule: "country_code_alpha_2 = UPPER(TRIM(country_code_alpha_2))"

            - rule: "country_code_alpha_2 ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: country_code_alpha_3
          data_type: VARCHAR(3)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "LENGTH(country_code_alpha_3) = 3"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_3 = UPPER(TRIM(country_code_alpha_3))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "country_code_alpha_3 ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'"

            - rule: "LENGTH(alpha2_country_code) = 2"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "alpha2_country_code = UPPER(TRIM(alpha2_country_code))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "regexp_matches(alpha2_country_code, '^[A-Z]{2}$')"

            - rule: "alpha2_country_code IN (SELECT country_code_alpha_2 FROM stg_customer360__country_codes)"
              on_failure: delete_row

    - name: stg_customer360__nicknames
